column3: 他の人が言ったことや尋ねたことを伝える。
column4: He said that he was tired.||She asked me where I lived.||The teacher told us to be quiet.
column5: 発言を伝えるときは時制や代名詞を文脈に合わせて変える。命令はtell + 人 + to不定詞で表す。
column6: He said that I am tired.||He said that he was tired.

column3: 関係節や副詞節を短く表現する。
column4: The woman sitting next to me is a lawyer.||Products made in the country are popular.||Having finished her work, she went home.
column5: 現在分詞は能動的な意味、過去分詞は受動的な意味を表すことが多い。主節の主語との関係に注意する。
column6: The woman sat next to me is a lawyer.||The woman sitting next to me is a lawyer.

column3: 現実とは異なる状態を望むことを表す。
column4: I wish I spoke English fluently.||She wishes she hadn't said that.||If only it would stop raining!
column5: 現在の願望には過去形、過去の後悔には過去完了を使う。wouldは変化を望む場合に使うことがある。
column6: I wish I speak English fluently.||I wish I spoke English fluently.

column2: 基本倒置（So / Neither、Not onlyなど）
column3: 「私も」「私もそうではない」を表したり、正式な文章で強調したりする。
column4: I love durian. So do I.||She didn't come. Neither did he.||Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
column5: So / Neitherの後ろでは助動詞を主語の前に置く。否定語を文頭に置くときも倒置が起こる。

column2: 助動詞の完了形（should have、must haveなど）
column3: 後悔を述べたり、過去について推測したりする。
column4: You should have told me earlier.||He must have forgotten the meeting.||She can't have finished already.
column5: 助動詞 + have + 過去分詞を使う。should haveは過去の後悔、must haveは強い推測を表す。
column6: He must has forgotten the meeting.||He must have forgotten the meeting.

column2: つなぎ言葉と談話標識
column3: 段落内の文と文の考えをつなぐ。
column4: The hotel was expensive. However, the service was excellent.||It rained heavily. As a result, the match was canceled.||Please reply by Friday. Otherwise, we will give the seat to someone else.
column5: howeverは対比、as a resultは結果、otherwiseは別の結果や条件を示す。
column6: The hotel was expensive, however the service was excellent.||The hotel was expensive. However, the service was excellent.

column3: 未来のある時点まで、一定期間続いている行動を表す。
column4: By June, I will have been working here for five years.||Next month, she will have been teaching for a decade.||By midnight, they will have been driving for eight hours.
column5: will have beenと動詞の-ing形を使い、未来の基準時までの継続期間に焦点を置く。
column6: By June, I will have working here for five years.||By June, I will have been working here for five years.

column3: 仕事や学術的な文章に出てくる長い名詞句を読み、組み立てる。
column4: our highly experienced sales team||a two-week training program||the company's annual performance review
column5: 中心となる名詞を見つけ、前置修飾語や所有格がどのように説明を加えるかを読む。
column6: a team sales highly experienced||our highly experienced sales team

column2: 仮定法（suggest that + 動詞原形）
column3: 正式な英語で、提案・要求・必要性を表す動詞や表現の後に使う。
column4: The doctor recommended that he rest for a week.||It is essential that every employee attend the meeting.||She insisted that we be on time.
column5: suggestやrecommendのthat節では主語に関係なく動詞原形を使う。
column6: The doctor recommended that he rests.||The doctor recommended that he rest.

column2: 分裂文（It is ... that / What ... is）
column3: 文の一部を特に強調する。
column4: It was my mother who taught me to cook.||What I love about the capital city is the food.||It is in the morning that I study best.
column5: It is ... thatやWhat ... isの形で、強調したい情報を文の前面に出す。
column6: It was my mother which taught me to cook.||It was my mother who taught me to cook.

column3: 正式な文章や難しい試験問題で使う。
column4: No sooner had I arrived than it started to rain.||Only after the meeting did I understand the plan.||Should you have any questions, please contact us.
column5: 否定・制限表現を文頭に置くと助動詞が主語の前に来る。no sooner ... thanは「～するとすぐに」を表す。
column6: Only after the meeting I did understand the plan.||Only after the meeting did I understand the plan.

column3: 同じ語の繰り返しを避け、自然に話したり書いたりする。
column4: Will it rain tomorrow? I hope not.||I don't like this shirt. Can I see the blue one?||She said she would call, and she did.
column5: 文脈から分かる語を省略したり、oneやdoなどで前の表現を代用したりする。
column6: I hope it will not rain tomorrow.||I hope not.

column3: 学術的な文章や丁寧な会話で、確信の度合いを示す。
column4: The results seem to suggest a link.||Prices are likely to rise next year.||I was wondering if you could help me.
column5: seem、likely、might、wouldなどを使って断定を避け、慎重または丁寧に述べる。
column6: The results prove a link.||The results seem to suggest a link.

column2: 正式な表現とくだけた表現
column3: 仕事のメール、応募書類、友人へのメッセージなど状況に合う言葉を選ぶ。
column4: Please do not hesitate to contact us.||We regret to inform you that the position has been filled.||Hey, can you send me that file?
column5: 相手や目的に合わせて語彙、挨拶、依頼表現の丁寧さを調整する。
column6: Hey, please submit the application immediately.||Please submit the application at your earliest convenience.
